items.title: Australia releases six days' worth of petrol from emergency stockpile
items.description: Australia will make available about six days' worth of petrol from its emergency stockpile and five days of diesel, the first use of its fuel reserves since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

items.title: Petrol prices are rising. This map shows why
items.description: Drones and missiles have landed on key refineries and depots, destroying millions of barrels of oil production. ABC NEWS Verify maps key locations destroyed or targeted during the war.

items.title: Live: Netanyahu makes veiled threat against Iran's new supreme leader
items.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds his first press conference since the war began and gives a veiled threat to kill Iran's new supreme leader. Follow live.

items.title: Running on empty — how we were caught short of oil
items.description: Australia is one of the biggest energy exporters on the planet, as the world's third-largest exporter of LNG and the biggest seaborne supplier of thermal and metallurgical coal. But when it comes to oil the country is horribly exposed.

items.title: Iran's war within a war may be about to begin
items.description: On Iraq's border with Iran, troops are amassing as Iranian Kurds from across the globe gather to revolt after 47 years of being the victims of an oppressive and cruel regime.

items.title: 'Move on and be a good corporate citizen for once', analyst tells Qantas
items.description: Qantas agrees to settle a class action ​related to flight credits issued during the COVID-19 ‌pandemic.

items.title: 'Didn't even have their passports': Activists fear for Iranian footballers
items.description: Iranian activists are racing against time to convince members of the country's female football team to turn back from Malaysia, as fears grow that the women are being coerced home by regime officials.

items.title: Ancestral remains returned to Country after a century in a British museum
items.description: After almost 130 years the remains of an Aboriginal man have made the long journey home from a museum in England. Now reburied on the Country from where he was taken at Berowra Creek in Sydney.

items.title: Trump's war tests his 'maybe less enthusiastic' VP Vance
items.description: From MAGA-loathing "hillbilly" to vice-president, JD Vance's rise and rebirth have been something to behold. But the war in Iran may test his considerable political dexterity.

items.title: Live: ASX up after fall on Wall Street as oil hits $US100 per barrel
items.description: The ASX 200 has defied expectations to post modest gains during its final trading day of the week. It came after the Dow Jones fell sharply overnight and as the price of oil hit $US100 a barrel. Follow the day's events and insights on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Daly River flood nearing worst on record, with more rain forecast
items.description: Flooding in the remote Northern Territory town of Daly River is edging closer to becoming the community's worst on record, with more rain forecast for parts of the Top End.

items.title: Byron Bay Bluesfest cancelled at short notice
items.description: Thousands of music fans will be left scrambling to rearrange their Easter plans after Byron Bay's famous Bluesfest was called off at short notice.

items.title: Search underway for Bundaberg man who disappeared from houseboat
items.description: Emergency Services are searching the flooded Burnett River in Bundaberg for a man believed to be missing from a houseboat, and have airlifted a woman bitten by a snake from her isolated home.

items.title: Australian businessman found guilty of reckless foreign interference
items.description: Australian businessman Alexander Csergo is found guilty of reckless foreign interference, after a Sydney court hears he compiled reports for two suspected Chinese spies while overseas.

items.title: From a new quiz show to a restaurant-worthy dish, we've got your weekend covered
items.description: This weekend try an unforgettable feta recipe or get lost in the hypnotic rhythms of legendary desert blues band Tinariwen's new album.

items.title: For a renowned actor, Hugo Weaving lives a very un-Hollywood life
items.description: Hugo Weaving may be an internationally renowned actor of both stage and screen, but he says he never feels ready for his next big role.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: A new Nationals leader and a curious crocodile
items.description: Think you've been paying attention to the news cycle this week? Test your memory here.

items.title: When the Matildas played in North Korea a full stadium laughed at them
items.description: When the Matildas played North Korea in Pyongyang in 2007, it was like unlike anything they had experienced before.

items.title: Loved one stuck inside the manosphere? Here's how to help
items.description: Don't panic, don't erupt, remain open and ask questions: Here are some of the tips from experts on how to reclaim a loved one from the manosphere.

items.title: Paralympians express disappointment over media coverage of winter Games
items.description: The Paralympic Winter Games are in full swing at Milano Cortina and athletes and supporters have expressed their frustration over the lack of coverage of the event.

items.title: Western Australia the big GST winner again, despite massive budget surpluses
items.description: WA will get an extra $6.6 billion from taxpayers in the coming financial year under its special GST deal, despite being the only state with a budget surplus.

items.title: Interruptions, campaign woes and 'razzle-dazzle': Here's how the SA leaders debate played out
items.description: As South Australians get ready to vote in a week's time, Premier Peter Malinauskas and Opposition Leader Ashton Hurn went head-to-head in a campaign debate. Here's what they said.

items.title: Controversy at Women's Asian Cup after former coach leads 'Taiwan' chant
items.description: The Women's Asian Cup has been embroiled in another diplomatic controversy, with Taiwanese officials lodging a complaint after a former national coach was ejected from a stadium for leading a chant which included the word "Taiwan."

items.title: Australia is experiencing a bunny boom. What's next for biocontrol?
items.description: With millions of feral rabbits currently hopping around the continent, you might wonder if the viruses that kept their numbers down in the past still work.

items.title: Father jailed for neglect of 7yo son who died of pneumonia and sepsis
items.description: A father who "prolonged his child's suffering" by failing to get him medical attention for 16 hours before his death, has been sentenced to 19 months in prison.
